text: See what your LLM calls cost. llmtee is a self-hosted proxy for the OpenAI and Anthropic APIs and for OpenAI-compatible providers such as OpenRouter, Ollama, vLLM and Groq. You point your client's base URL at it, and it logs every request with tokens, cost, latency and time to first token. Like the Unix tee , it passes each response through to your client unchanged and keeps a copy. llmtee is built for individuals and small teams who want to see and cap their LLM spend. It is not a gateway with routing, fallbacks or multi-tenancy. The current release is 0.x, so configuration may still change between minor versions. docker run -d --name llmtee -p 8080:8080 -v llmtee-data:/data \ -e LLMTEE_ADMIN_PASSWORD=change-me ghcr.io/garritfra/llmtee Point your client at llmtee. It forwards your provider key unchanged: export OPENAI_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8080/openai/v1 export ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8080/anthropic Send any request, then open http://localhost:8080 and sign in with the admin password. The request appears in the list with its tokens and cost. Without Docker, download a binary from the releases (Linux, macOS and Windows on amd64 and arm64) and run LLMTEE_ADMIN_PASSWORD=change-me ./llmtee . llmtee creates llmtee.db in the current directory. Other setups: docker-compose.yml , PostgreSQL compose , systemd unit , Caddy with TLS . The Setup page in the web UI shows how to connect Claude Code, Codex, opencode and Pi, with your instance's base URL filled in. Guides for these agents, the SDKs, Ollama, OpenRouter, vLLM and n8n are in docs/integrations.md . llmtee logs chat completions, responses, embeddings and Anthropic messages, streamed or not. It forwards all other paths without logging them. Details are in docs/headers.md . llmtee works with two kinds of keys, and you can use both at once. A provider key is your OpenAI, Anthropic or other API key. By default, clients send it as usual and llmtee forwards it. llmtee stores only its SHA-256 hash, as a key id starting with pt- . To give a provider key a name and a budget, label it in the UI or with llmtee keys label . A llmtee key ( llmtee-… ) replaces the provider key on the client side. llmtee swaps in the real provider key from OPENAI_API_KEY , ANTHROPIC_API_KEY , OPENROUTER_API_KEY or LLMTEE_UPSTREAM_<NAME>_API_KEY , so teammates and agents never see it. Create one in the UI or on the command line: llmtee keys create hermes-agent --budget-day 5 --budget-month 60 llmtee keys list A client can also send a llmtee key next to its provider key, in a Llmtee-Key header, to attribute its requests to that key. To reject all requests without a valid llmtee key, set LLMTEE_REQUIRE_PROXY_KEY=true . llmtee checks budgets in memory before it forwards a request. A key at or over its limit gets a 429 response in the provider's error format, with a Retry-After header. Limits reset at the start of the next UTC day or month. llmtee only knows the cost of a request after the response arrives. The request that crosses the limit therefore completes, and a key can overshoot its budget by that one request. To tag requests with a user, session or custom property, or to skip storing a body, see docs/headers.md . client ──► router ─► auth + budget ─► forwarder ─► upstream ▲ │ (tee) └──── stream, unbuffered ──┤ ▼ copy usage parser ─► pricing ─► batch writer ─► SQLite / PostgreSQL ─► UI, /metrics, MCP Only routing, the in-memory key and budget check, and forwarding happen while the client waits. llmtee writes and flushes each chunk to the client as soon as it arrives, and passes a copy to a usage parser. Golden tests replay recorded OpenAI and Anthropic streams through the proxy and require byte-identical output. Pricing, budget updates, metrics and database writes run in the background, in batches every 500 ms or 100 events. If the database is slow or unavailable, llmtee still forwards requests. It drops the log events and counts them in llmtee_events_dropped_total . On an Apple M4 Pro at 200 requests per second against a local fake upstream, llmtee added 0.14 ms at p50 and 0.02 ms at p99, and used about 33 MB of memory. You can reproduce this with make loadtest . The tradeoff is that llmtee sits in the request path. If it is down, your LLM calls fail. Monitor /healthz and keep the provider's direct base URL at hand as a fallback. For OpenAI chat streams, llmtee adds stream_options.include_usage: true if the client did not, so the stream ends with a usage chunk. You can turn this off with LLMTEE_INJECT_STREAM_USAGE=false . If a response contains no usage, llmtee marks the request as "usage unknown". It never estimates tokens. Prices come from LiteLLM's price table , embedded at build time and refreshed weekly. llmtee stores the cost with each request, so later price changes do not alter past requests. To add prices for local or private models, see docs/configuration.md . llmtee reads its settings from environment variables or a YAML file. The settings you are most likely to need: All settings, including retention, redaction, alerts and running several instances against PostgreSQL, are in docs/configuration.md . Body logging is on by default with 30-day retention, so you can inspect the exact prompt and response behind each cost. Bodies can contain personal or confidential data. You can turn body logging off globally ( LLMTEE_LOG_BODIES=false ), per upstream, or per request with the Llmtee-Omit-* headers. LLMTEE_REDACT_FIELDS replaces named JSON fields before storage. llmtee never writes provider keys to the database, only their SHA-256 hashes. It sends no telemetry. Web UI at / : spend today and this month compared with the previous period, a cost chart that can be split by model, key, user or upstream, budget meters, a filterable request list and request details with bodies. The pages are rendered on the server with Go templates and htmx. CSV export : the Export CSV button exports the current filter, or run llmtee export --range 30d > requests.csv . Prometheus at /metrics : request, token and cost counters, request duration, time to first token, budget rejections and dropped events. Send Authorization: Bearer <admin password> . Health at /healthz : returns 200 with {"status":"ok"} while the proxy runs. MCP at /mcp (streamable HTTP, Authorization: Bearer <admin password> ): tools get_spend , list_requests and get_request . To add it to Claude Code: claude mcp add --transport http llmtee http://localhost:8080/mcp --header " Authorization: Bearer $LLMTEE_ADMIN_PASSWORD " Compared to llmtee Helicone (self-hosted) Langfuse LiteLLM Proxy Integration base URL base URL SDK / OpenTelemetry base URL Services to run 1 binary (+ optional Postgres) several containers web, worker, Postgres, ClickHouse, Redis, S3 proxy + Postgres for spend tracking Hard budgets per key yes cost-based rate-limit policies via headers no yes Status active maintenance mode since March 2026 active active Scope logging, cost, budgets logging, analytics tracing, evals, prompts gateway: 100+ providers, routing, fallbacks If you need evals, prompt management, routing or fallbacks, use one of the others. Moving from Helicone is covered in docs/migrating-from-helicone.md . make test # unit, golden and end-to-end tests (SQLite) make test-postgres # storage tests against PostgreSQL make integration # official Python and TypeScript SDKs against the proxy make loadtest # added latency vs. a fake upstream (needs vegeta) make prices # refresh the embedded price table scripts/record-golden.sh re-records the golden streams from the real APIs. See CONTRIBUTING.md . Apache-2.0 . The embedded price data comes from LiteLLM (MIT).
